coverage.stoppingReason: Stopped after four evidence-rich priority cases, one stress comparator, the principal USDX name collision, and ancestry triage; historical parameter-by-height, bridge inventories, quantitative peg series, and several later outcomes remain queued.

eligibility.reason: Deployed in 2019 and materially active throughout 2020-2021.

versions.label: MCD with Liquidations 1.x
versions.tokenRoles: DAI is transferable debt money; MKR governs and is a dilution backstop.
versions.backing: Governance-approved vault collateral, with borrower excess subordinate to debt; system surplus and MKR dilution backstop shortfall.
versions.redemption: No ordinary holder claim on a named reserve; market sale and borrower repayment, with proportional collateral claim only after Emergency Shutdown.
versions.supplyPolicy: Vault draw mints and repayment burns within collateral debt ceilings; governance changes rates and ceilings.
versions.debtAndIncentives: Stability fees, DSR, collateral auctions, keeper profit and MKR debt/surplus auctions.
versions.oracle: Governance-selected feeds pass through a one-hour Oracle Security Module delay.
versions.governanceAndAdmin: MKR governance controls collateral, risk parameters, oracle sets, spells and shutdown subject to security mechanisms.
versions.liquidityDependencies: DAI markets, keeper-held DAI, Ethereum inclusion and auction participation.

versions.label: MCD with PSM and Liquidations 2.0
versions.tokenRoles: DAI and MKR as above; PSM reserve stablecoins become direct swap inventory.
versions.backing: Vault collateral plus governance-controlled PSM assets including centralized stablecoins.
versions.redemption: Fixed-price PSM swaps subject to fees/limits; Emergency Shutdown remains final settlement.
versions.supplyPolicy: PSM can expand/contract DAI against accepted stablecoin inventory; vault policy remains governed.
versions.debtAndIncentives: Dutch collateral auctions record bad debt in Vow and include keeper incentives; surplus precedes MKR dilution.
versions.oracle: Governed oracle stack; centralized PSM collateral adds issuer/custodian/freeze dependence.
versions.governanceAndAdmin: MKR governance configures PSM fees/ceilings and liquidation parameters.
versions.liquidityDependencies: PSM collateral liquidity, keepers, DEX/CEX markets and Ethereum execution.

incidents.summary: Price collapse and Ethereum congestion coincided with zero/near-zero collateral-auction bids and protocol bad debt.
incidents.lossBearers: Liquidated vault owners, system surplus and ultimately MKR holders through recapitalization
incidents.outcome: Debt auctions and later liquidation/peg-support redesigns.

eligibility.reason: First-party manifest dates deployment to 2021-04-05 inside the window.

lineage.relationship: later redesign, not the same stablecoin

versions.label: Liquity v1 immutable core
versions.tokenRoles: LUSD is debt and redemption token; LQTY rewards Stability Pool/frontends and receives protocol fees when staked.
versions.backing: ETH locked in borrower Troves, plus LUSD deposited voluntarily in the Stability Pool as liquidation capacity.
versions.redemption: Any holder can exchange LUSD for $1 of ETH, less fee, against lowest-collateralized Troves.
versions.supplyPolicy: Trove borrowing mints; repayment, redemption and Stability Pool liquidation burn LUSD; dynamic one-off fees react to redemptions.
versions.debtAndIncentives: 110% MCR; gas compensation; Stability Pool offset first, then redistribution to active Troves; Recovery Mode below 150% TCR.
versions.oracle: Immutable deployed PriceFeed mediates ETH/USD with configured fallback logic; no governance parameter changes.
versions.governanceAndAdmin: Core contracts are represented by the project as immutable and governance-free after deployment.
versions.liquidityDependencies: Ethereum inclusion, liquidators, Stability Pool depth and external LUSD markets/frontends.

incidents.summary: Liquity v2/BOLD documentation describes removal of v1 Recovery Mode and different branch shutdown controls; LUSD v1 remains a separate legacy system.
incidents.outcome: Later design changed controls without retroactively changing v1.

eligibility.reason: sUSD and Synthetix v2 were materially active in the window; dated SIPs specify relevant controls.

versions.label: Synthetix v2 pooled debt
versions.tokenRoles: sUSD is a synth and debt-repayment unit; SNX is collateral, governance/incentive token and liquidation asset.
versions.backing: Locked SNX backs a pooled synthetic debt whose value changes with the synth portfolio.
versions.redemption: Issuers burn sUSD against their debt; other holders rely on synth exchange and markets rather than unconditional $1 collateral redemption.
versions.supplyPolicy: SNX stakers issue/burn synth debt subject to issuance ratio; synth exchanges burn source and issue destination.
versions.debtAndIncentives: Fees/rewards motivate target ratios; delayed partial liquidation burns liquidator sUSD for discounted SNX.
versions.oracle: Chainlink pricing, waiting/reclaim logic and circuit breakers; oracle latency can transfer value to traders.
versions.governanceAndAdmin: Configurable ratios, penalties, fees, oracle/exchange settings and system suspension through protocol governance/owner machinery.
versions.liquidityDependencies: SNX liquidity, synth AMMs, liquidators, oracle updates and exchange integrators.

versions.label: Ethereum/Optimism debt synthesis proposal
versions.backing: SNX collateral and pooled debt intended to be measured across chains.
versions.redemption: No new unconditional par redemption specified.
versions.supplyPolicy: Issuance relies on oracle-reported total debt and debt-share ratios across chains.
versions.debtAndIncentives: Rewards and fees remain chain-sensitive while debt responsibility becomes global.
versions.oracle: Common Chainlink debt synthesis oracles report cross-chain aggregates.
versions.governanceAndAdmin: SIP-governed implementation and cross-chain fee-period messages.
versions.liquidityDependencies: Ethereum, Optimism, common oracle availability and Optimism Messenger/cross-chain broadcaster.

incidents.summary: Legacy EtherCollateral loan contracts were sunset; after notice, third parties could repay debt and claim remaining collateral.
incidents.outcome: Legacy collateral products deprecated in favor of newer multicollateral loans.

eligibility.reason: Native Kava CDP stablecoin was materially active and supplies a non-Ethereum/cross-chain comparator.

lineage.relationship: CDP and auction-mechanism comparator, not issuer lineage

versions.label: Kava CDP/auction modules
versions.tokenRoles: USDX is native debt/auction coin; KAVA governs, secures consensus and is minted in debt auctions.
versions.backing: Collateral locked in Kava CDPs, including representations of source-chain assets such as BNB.
versions.redemption: Borrowers repay/burn USDX to unlock collateral; no general holder par redemption found.
versions.supplyPolicy: CDP draw mints within debt limits; repayment and successful liquidations burn; savings and fees are governed.
versions.debtAndIncentives: Collateral auctions sell seized assets for USDX; residual bad debt triggers KAVA-minting debt auctions after thresholds.
versions.oracle: Pricefeed module and governance-set spot/liquidation market IDs; missing prices suspend risk-changing operations.
versions.governanceAndAdmin: Kava governance controls collateral, ratios, fees, limits and auction thresholds; validators secure application-chain state.
versions.liquidityDependencies: Funded USDX auction bots, Kava execution, source-chain gateways/custody, pricefeeds and secondary USDX liquidity.

eligibility.reason: Active in 2020-2021 and supplies a documented peg and bad-debt stress comparator.

versions.label: 2020-2021 VAI
versions.tokenRoles: VAI is borrower-minted stable debt; XVS governs and was proposed as a loss backstop.
versions.backing: Venus account collateral capacity; exact deployed-version constraints not fully reconstructed.
versions.redemption: Repayment and secondary markets; no unconditional $1 collateral redemption established by reviewed evidence.
versions.supplyPolicy: Governed minting and later proposed stability fee; mint pause proposed in September 2021.
versions.debtAndIncentives: Venus liquidators seize collateral; prospective risk-fund/XVS mechanisms address shortfall.
versions.oracle: Venus price oracle; exact 2021 VAI oracle implementation unresolved.
versions.governanceAndAdmin: Governance can pause minting and alter controller/fee parameters.
versions.liquidityDependencies: BNB Smart Chain, liquidators, VAI venues and borrower repayment demand.

incidents.summary: XVS price manipulation and subsequent liquidations produced a Venus shortfall; exact audited amount was not established here.
incidents.beneficiaries: Accounts able to borrow against inflated collateral
incidents.lossBearers: Protocol liquidity and, under later proposals, risk-fund/XVS stakeholders
incidents.outcome: Governance proposed a layered shortfall coverage framework.

incidents.summary: Venus team acknowledged serious VAI oversupply and proposed halting minting.
incidents.beneficiaries: VAI debtors able to repurchase below par
incidents.lossBearers: Market buyers and liquidity providers exposed to discount
incidents.outcome: Mint pause and stability-fee plan discussed.

eligibility.reason: Historically active namesake but a basket/meta-stablecoin rather than Kava's CDP USDX; retained to prevent issuer conflation.

versions.label: 2020 dForce USDx basket
versions.tokenRoles: USDx represented an indexed/basket stable asset.
versions.backing: Constituent fiat-backed stablecoins according to project materials.
versions.redemption: Constituent conversion mechanics were not fully reconstructed.
versions.governanceAndAdmin: Basket weights/governance described by project materials; exact powers unresolved.
versions.liquidityDependencies: Constituent stablecoins, their issuers/custodians and Ethereum liquidity.

claims.statement: MCD DAI is a USD soft peg generated against governance-approved excess collateral; ordinary holders obtain direct collateral claims only through Emergency Shutdown.
claims.evidenceLocator: Whitepaper: Price Stability Mechanisms, Emergency Shutdown; deployment output
claims.reasoning: Primary design and deployment evidence align.
claims.uncertainty: Exact parameter history varies by governance spell.

claims.statement: MKR governance controlled risk parameters and oracle selection; surplus precedes MKR dilution as the ultimate recapitalization mechanism.
claims.evidenceLocator: Risk Management; Key External Actors; MKR and MCD

claims.statement: On 2020-03-12, congestion and deficient keeper bidding allowed zero/near-zero auction outcomes and bad debt, showing liquidation execution can defeat nominal overcollateralization.
claims.evidenceLocator: MIP45 motivation contrasts Liquidations 1.2 with redesign
claims.reasoning: MIP45 establishes the auction redesign and bad-debt pathway; exact loss total intentionally omitted because no retrieved primary quantified it here.
claims.uncertainty: A dedicated first-party postmortem should be added for full event quantification.

claims.statement: Liquidations 2.0 uses Dog to confiscate unsafe vaults, record bad debt in Vow and initiate Dutch Clipper auctions with keeper incentives.
claims.uncertainty: Per-collateral activation dates not enumerated.

claims.statement: The PSM improves fixed-price arbitrage but converts issuer, freeze and custody risk of accepted stablecoins into DAI backing risk.
claims.evidenceLocator: MIP45 references PSM/stablecoin collateral; whitepaper recognizes centralized collateral control
claims.reasoning: Economic inference from direct stablecoin inventory and issuer control.
claims.uncertainty: The exact activation spell and fee settings were not retrieved.

claims.statement: Liquity v1 deployed on Ethereum on 2021-04-05; the manifest identifies LUSD and core contract addresses and code version.
claims.uncertainty: Explorer bytecode not independently compared.

claims.statement: Liquity v1 accepted only ETH and represented its core as immutable and governance-free.
claims.evidenceLocator: General FAQ; repository definitions and ownership discussion
claims.reasoning: First-party documentation and code architecture claim.
claims.uncertainty: No independent authority graph was generated.

claims.statement: Any LUSD holder could redeem at face value for ETH against lowest-collateralized Troves, subject to a dynamic redemption fee.
claims.reasoning: Mechanism documented in two first-party sources.

claims.statement: Below 110% MCR, liquidation burns Stability Pool LUSD for ETH; uncovered debt and collateral redistribute to active Troves.
claims.evidenceLocator: Stability Pool FAQ; repository Definitions: Liquidation

claims.statement: Recovery Mode activates below 150% TCR, blocks worsening borrower actions and expands liquidation eligibility.
sUSD was backed economically by locked SNX and pooled synthetic debt, not by an unconditional holder claim on $1 of collateral.
claims.reasoning: SIP explains collateral, debt, incentives and lack of prior direct redemption.
claims.uncertainty: Full historical debt-pool accounting code was not version-pinned.

claims.statement: SIP-15 liquidations use delayed flagging and partial sUSD burn for discounted SNX; below collateral plus penalty a shortfall can remain.
claims.uncertainty: Live parameter values changed by SCCP.

claims.statement: SIP-120 combined Chainlink and Uniswap v3 prices with caps and volatility breakers and acknowledged oracle-latency strategies could profit at debt-pool expense.
claims.uncertainty: Precise activation transaction not checked.

claims.statement: SIP-165 proposed merging Ethereum and Optimism debt pools using common Chainlink debt oracles and cross-chain messaging.
claims.uncertainty: End-of-window proposal; deployment chronology unresolved.

claims.statement: Kava USDX is a native Kava coin minted by CDPs and described as loosely USD-pegged with price determined by markets.
claims.evidenceLocator: Native assets; What is a CDP?
claims.uncertainty: Page is current and not archived to a 2020 version.

claims.statement: For BNB collateral, BNB was frozen/unfrozen on Binance Chain while representations were minted/burned on Kava.
claims.uncertainty: Operator/key architecture was not recovered.

claims.statement: Kava CDPs use governed liquidation ratios, fees, limits and pricefeed market IDs; absent prices suspend both liquidation and risk-changing operations.
claims.evidenceLocator: CDP module interactions/dependency pricefeed; parameter table
claims.uncertainty: Examples are not proven historical mainnet values.

claims.statement: Kava collateral auctions require USDX bidders and use forward then reverse phases, returning excess collateral to the CDP owner.
claims.evidenceLocator: Auction Concepts; Auction Bot How Auctions Work
claims.uncertainty: Actual bidder concentration not measured.

claims.statement: Residual CDP debt can trigger auctions that mint KAVA for USDX, making KAVA holders/governors the final dilution backstop.
claims.evidenceLocator: Liquidation & Stability System; Debt Auction definition
claims.uncertainty: No historical debt-auction execution was identified.

claims.statement: On 2021-09-08 the Venus team acknowledged serious VAI oversupply, reported USD:VAI above 1.3:1 and proposed pausing minting.
claims.uncertainty: Ratio not independently reproduced.

claims.statement: VAI's persistent discount despite claimed excess collateral shows collateral accounting did not provide sufficient holder-side peg demand.
claims.evidenceLocator: Team explanation of supply exceeding demand
claims.reasoning: Inference from the project's own diagnosis and lack of evidenced par redemption.
claims.uncertainty: A full market microstructure study was not performed.

claims.statement: Venus proposed covering shortfall first with a risk fund, then up to 10% of XVS vault deposits, unissued XVS, and finally bonds.
claims.reasoning: Direct proposal text, explicitly treated as prospective.
claims.uncertainty: Implementation and funding status not established.

claims.statement: dForce USDx was a 2020 Ethereum basket/meta-stablecoin and is not Kava's native CDP USDX; later dForce USX is also distinct.
claims.reasoning: Issuer and mechanism differ from Kava sources.
claims.uncertainty: Exact basket/deployment history not reconstructed.

claims.statement: Liquity v2 documentation says v1 Recovery Mode was removed and replaced with different branch safety/shutdown controls.
claims.evidenceLocator: Why was Recovery Mode removed?; Shutdown Mode
claims.reasoning: Later first-party comparison, used only as hindsight.
claims.uncertainty: Publication date unavailable.

claims.statement: Synthetix announced legacy EtherCollateral loan deprecation on 2021-05-25 and liquidation of remaining loans after 2021-06-25.
claims.uncertainty: Execution transactions not checked.
